summary: Golem is a dense engine-building euro where you grow a golem's power through careful action drafting on a marble-based turn order system, balancing risk against reward since an overgrown golem can rampage and hurt you. Every round is a tight puzzle of sequencing actions, managing resources, and timing when to cash in your golem's power before it becomes a liability.
praised: Clever marble-drafting turn order mechanism that ties action selection to when you act
Strong engine-building depth with meaningful variable player powers
High replayability from variable setup and multiple viable strategies
Satisfying tension between growing the golem and controlling it before it turns destructive
criticised: Steep rules overhead and long teach for a first play
Heavy on fiddly bookkeeping and tracking many resource types
Player interaction is limited and mostly indirect
Can feel like a solitaire, multiplayer-solitaire experience at lower player counts

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light blocking over shared action spaces and turn order

scoring.why: Points accumulate from golem development, artifacts, book collection, and end-game bonuses, rewarding whoever builds the most efficient overall engine
